case.presentation: A 27-year-old woman has had persistently mild thrombocytopenia for 3 years, with platelet counts ranging from about 100k to 150k per microliter. Her count is currently 110k. She reports that the low counts first appeared after a postpartum hemorrhage. She has no history of liver disease, splenomegaly, transfusions, or a family history of blood disorders. Other blood counts, kidney function, and basic labs have been unremarkable. What is the recommended management for her thrombocytopenia?
case.recommendations: The most likely diagnosis is chronic mild immune thrombocytopenia. The recommended work-up includes HIV and hepatitis C antibody, Vitamin B12 level, a complete blood count with differential (using a citrate tube for platelets), a peripheral blood smear review, a basic chemistry panel, coagulation studies (PT, PTT, fibrinogen), von Willebrand screen (von Willebrand factor antigen and activity levels, factor VIII activity), and a hemolysis screen (LDH, haptoglobin, reticulocyte count), plus a pregnancy test if applicable. If any of these tests return abnormal, please notify hematology for possible in-person evaluation. If all results are normal, no specific treatment is needed; the patient can be monitored with an annual platelet count and should be counseled on bleeding signs (such as petechiae or heavy menstrual bleeding) and instructed to seek evaluation if these occur. Referral to hematology if the platelet count decreases significantly.
